summary: Reviewed the dispatcher, spawn-target resolution, dashboard boot test, and runtime-file coverage. One P1 exists: the patch protects Git commits but leaves a sensitive checkpoint file able to enter Docker image layers; the dashboard path fix itself is sound.

findings.title: Runtime-file check misses Docker image leakage of checkpoint data
findings.what: The new coverage verifies only Git ignore rules, while the repository's Docker build uses `COPY . .` and `.dockerignore` does not exclude `state.json.checkpoint` or `state.json.checkpoint.tmp`. Those files contain the broker checkpoint/history associated with the user's PII and can be copied into a built or published image.
findings.trigger: Run an opt-out pass, then build the documented Docker image from that checkout and push/share the image or its layers.
findings.impact: A Docker registry or anyone with access to the image can recover the user's broker-related run history, despite the patch's claim that runtime files cannot be committed or shipped.
findings.fix: Add `state.json.checkpoint` and `state.json.checkpoint.tmp` to `.dockerignore`, and extend the runtime-file test to validate both Git and Docker ignore coverage.
